subject: Use when designing or reviewing Next.js Route Handlers (the `route.ts`/`route.js` file convention in App Router): when…

evals.prompt: Define route-handler-design in 2-3 sentences. Include the work it owns and the kind of user request that should activate it.
Explain why an agent would need the route-handler-design skill instead of relying on generic reasoning. Name the failure it prevents.
Describe the mental model or main primitives behind route-handler-design. Keep it operational rather than just naming the topic.

A user asks: "design an internal create-comment form mutation triggered only from this app's UI (use server-actions-design)". Should route-handler-design activate? Explain the boundary and name the better owner when possible.
evals.negative_expectation: Must not force route-handler-design onto a request it explicitly excludes or that belongs to http-semantics, webhook-integration, streaming-architecture, client-server-boundary, server-actions-design, api-design, middleware-patterns, code-review.

evals.prompt: A user asks: "design the route.ts that receives a Stripe webhook — verify signature before parsing the body, return 200 immediately, queue the heavy work". Show the first concrete steps an agent should take when applying route-handler-design.

Place route-handler-design among its adjacent skills (http-semantics, webhook-integration, streaming-architecture, client-server-boundary, server-actions-design, api-design, middleware-patterns, code-review). What does it own, and what does it verify with or defer to?
evals.negative_expectation: Must not collapse related skills into interchangeable names; ownership must be mechanism-level.

evals.prompt: Name one plausible misconception about route-handler-design and correct it with a mechanism-level explanation.
